emerging_technology: Post-quantum cryptography migration for constrained connected devices
intended_application: Pilot a cryptographic-agility upgrade for a noncritical population of connected utility meters in a lab environment.
business_need: Protect long-lived infrastructure while preserving availability and device interoperability.
users_stakeholders: Security engineers, meter vendor, utility operations, customers
capabilities_constraints: Assume a device inventory and test lab; firmware update capacity, vendor support and protocol compatibility are incomplete.
risk_consequence_context: A failed update could disrupt metering; long-lived data and credentials may face future cryptographic risk.
management_question: Which migration path should be tested in 2027 without disrupting field operations?
additional_context: Hypothetical teaching case created 2026-11-16 for a prospective 2027 decision; organizational details and the proposed monitoring trigger are assumptions, not observations or forecasts. Conventional baseline: Existing public-key cryptography with inventory, segmentation and upgrade planning. Complement or dependency: Crypto-agile firmware, tested update mechanisms and vendor support. Proposed monitoring trigger and owner: Security lead reviews standards and vendor roadmaps quarterly; revisit when validated device interoperability, recovery and performance meet predefined lab requirements or standards guidance changes. Hype-sensitive assertion to test, not a fact: A standardized algorithm makes every device instantly quantum-safe.
